displayName: loop-sessions: ingest rejections in more than 10% of batches for 15 min

conditions.displayName: batches with a rejected item over all batches above 10% for 15 min

documentation.content:
More than a tenth of /v1/events batches carried an item the server refused for good, for fifteen minutes. A rejection is final on the laptop: the client quarantines the item with the server's reason in the file name and records a `rejected:<reason>` drop, so a rejection rate is captured work that will never be stored.

Read the reasons first: `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="loop-sessions" AND jsonPayload.message="ingest item rejected"' --freshness=1h --format='value(jsonPayload.reason,jsonPayload.event_type,jsonPayload.email,jsonPayload.device_id)' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. `no_session_id` and `no_id` are a client bug on the `agent_version` the `ingest_batches` metric labels the batches with; `batch_too_big` is a cap mismatch between that client and the server; a `scrub` reason is the server refusing content the laptop should have scrubbed. Then open the device on /admin/fleet: the quarantine row for that person carries the verb (`loop-sessions doctor --replay-quarantine` posts one item and prints the verdict).

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-quarantine
